summary:
[  edit  ]
The DMX In  CHOP  receives channels from DMX,  Art-Net ,  sACN  or  KiNET  devices. Channel values for DMX are 0-255. Note that input rate is limited to the DMX maximum refresh rate of 44Hz.
A Filter Table can be provided in a  DAT  where addresses can be specified by adding rows for each channel and specifying  net ,  subnet  and  universe . Optionally, packets can be filtered using the  srcaddress  and  destaddress  columns; only packets that have a matching source IP address and destination IP address will be accepted. The cell values for these columns should be a single IP address (ie.  Pattern Matching   not  supported); if left blank then all packets will be accepted.
The  srcaddress  column is useful for when there is DMX noise on the network that needs to be filtered out; the IP of the desired controller can be specified in the  srcaddress  cell. The  id  column should be used in conjunction with  srcaddress  and  destaddress  to provide a unique channel suffix.
Wireshark  is a useful tool for debugging network issues. In the Art-Net case, packets can easily be filtered using  artnet ,  dmx , or  dmx_chan .
ENTTEC NOTE:  - Use ENTTEC's  NMU (Node Management Utility)  to configure and inspect the ENTTEC devices found on your network.
See also:  DMX Out POP ,  Art-Net ,  DMX Out CHOP ,  DMX

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Connects to the device while On.

parameters.label: Interface
parameters.name: interface
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the type of interface to connect to the device with.

parameters.label: Enttec Generic Serial
parameters.name: serial
parameters.description: Uses the operating system's serial calls to read data.

parameters.label: Art-Net
parameters.name: artnet
parameters.description: Sets the interface to  Art-Net  protocol.

parameters.label: sACN
parameters.name: sacn
parameters.description: Sets the interface to  sACN  protocol.

parameters.label: KiNET
parameters.name: kinet
parameters.description: Sets the interface to  KiNET  protocol.

parameters.label: KiNET Version
parameters.name: kinetversion
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the version of the KiNET protocol to use.

parameters.label: Device
parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Select a DMX device from the menu.

parameters.label: Serial Port
parameters.name: serialport
parameters.description: When the  Interface  parameter is set Generic Serial this parameter lets you select which Serial (COM) port to use.

parameters.label: Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between receiving Packet Per Sample (Timesliced), Packet Per Channel (Latest) or Packet Per Channel (All). When selecting Packet Per Channel (Latest), any messages outside the last cook are being discarded while the option Packet Per Channel (All) will append channels that would get otherwise skipped by dropped frames.

parameters.label: Art-Net Net (0-127)
parameters.name: net
parameters.description: When the  Interface  parameter is set to Art-Net, this sets the net address. A net is a groups of 16 consecutive subnets or 256 consecutive universes. The range for this parameter is 0-127. This is  not  a network IP address.

parameters.label: Art-Net Subnet (0-15)
parameters.name: subnet
parameters.description: When the  Interface  parameter is set to Art-Net, this sets the subnet address. A subnet is a group of 16 consecutive universes. The range for this parameter is 0-15. This is  not  a network subnet mask.

parameters.label: Art-Net Universe (0-15)
parameters.name: universe
parameters.description: When the  Interface  parameter is set to Art-Net, this sets the universe address. A single DMX512 frame of 512 channels is referred to as a universe. The range for this parameter is 0-15.

parameters.label: Filter Table
parameters.name: filterdat
parameters.description: Available when using Packet Per Channel Format for Art-Net or sACN. Use the docked  Table DAT  to specify which net, subnet, universe channels are being received from.

parameters.label: Net Name
parameters.name: netname
parameters.description: Specify the channel prefix for the net part of the address.

parameters.label: Subnet Name
parameters.name: subnetname
parameters.description: Specify the channel prefix for the subnet part of the address.

parameters.label: Universe Name
parameters.name: universename
parameters.description: Specify the channel prefix for the universe part of the address.

parameters.label: KiNET Port Name
parameters.name: kinetportname
parameters.description: Specify the channel prefix for the KiNET port part of the address.

parameters.label: Start Codes
parameters.name: startcodes
parameters.description: A list of accepted start codes when using sACN. If the DMX In  CHOP  receives an sACN packet with a start code not in the list then it will discard it.

parameters.label: Multicast
parameters.name: multicast
parameters.description: Enable multicast for sACN. Multicast automatically builds the IP based on Net, Subnet, and Universe of the device. This allows for the DMX In  CHOP  to automatically receive from a sender without knowledge of it's address.

parameters.label: Queue Size
parameters.name: queuesize
parameters.description: When using interface Art-Net or sACN, this will set the size of the incoming packets queue.  This can be used to smooth data, though latency will be higher.  In the case of Packet Per Channel (All), this parameter controls the maximum number of packets created per cook.

parameters.label: Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: Resample the incoming data to this rate.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: length

parameters.label: time_slice

parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.
